subject: Request: rollout kill-switch authorization for FastPay canary (SLA protection)
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@fastpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: FastPay canary — request for auto-pause + pin as SLA guard

Marissa,

Quick context: we’re starting a canary rollout of FastPay checkout scoring v2 next week (goal: reduce latency on embedding lookups). Given this workload touches payment surface, our SREs are asking for an operational "kill-switch" that will automatically pause traffic to the new variant and revert (pin) to the last stable model if error or P95 latency exceed thresholds during the canary window.

Specifically we are asking Redwood to:
- Enable an automatic pause (30s window) if 5xx rate > 0.3% for 5 consecutive minutes OR P95 latency for token generation > 850ms for 3 consecutive minutes.
- When triggered, automatically pin traffic back to the previous stable model for at least 60 minutes (manual unpin required or explicit approval).
- Grant a temporary SLA carve-out/exception for the first 72-hour canary so we can execute this failover behavior without breaching the standard rollout policy.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can authorize this behavior for FastPay, and what approvals you need from your side? We can loop in procurement/legal if a short amendment is required.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Gupta
Engineering Manager, Reliability
FastPay

---
Attachment: canary-requirements.csv (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@fastpay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FastPay canary — request for auto-pause + pin as SLA guard

Samir — thanks for the clear ask. I’ve looped in Laura (Head of Trust) and Jordan (Product Ops) so we can evaluate the safety net and sign off on the temporary exception. High level response: this is operationally feasible, but we need to lock down the exact thresholds, the duration of the pinned window, and the telemetry hooks we’ll use to trigger the action.

Proposal (short):
- Autorun conditions: 5xx > 0.3% over a rolling 5m window OR P95 latency > 850ms over a rolling 3m window (matches your ask).
- Automatic action: immediate traffic pause + traffic reroute to stable variant and apply a 60-minute mandatory pin.
- Observation window: 72-hour canary with continuous monitoring by both FastPay SRE and Redwood CS.
- Rollback notice: automated Slack + email to on-call lists; Redwood will not auto-resume traffic until manual release or consensus (wanted by SREs).

Attachments: I’ve attached an SLA exception form and a simple diagram of the planned control flow. Please sign the DocuSign link in this thread (linked below) so we can capture the amendment.

Questions for Laura/Jordan: what risk controls do we need on the Redwood side to avoid false positives (e.g., transient infra noise)? Also, will this require a temporary billing or token-count carve-out?

Next steps: Laura/Jordan — can you review and, if acceptable, confirm so we can push this through a short emergency approval?

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Exec (Strategic) | Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla-exception-form.pdf, canary-fallback-diagram.png
DocuSign: https://docusign.com/req/FP-2345/kill-switch

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@fastpay.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FastPay canary — request for auto-pause + pin as SLA guard

Thanks — reviewed. I’m supportive with the following risk controls to reduce the chance of an unnecessary failover:

1) Dual-signal gating: require both error-rate AND telemetry anomaly (spike in model confidence variance or large delta in token output size) OR sustained latency breach for the full 3m window before triggering.
2) Backoff hysteresis: if an autorun triggers and unblocks within 30m, require a manual check before another automatic trigger within the next 2 hours.
3) Telemetry checklist: confirm that FastPay will surface request IDs and sample payloads to a secure S3 (or share with our cs-team) for post-mortem.
4) Billing note: if pinning causes additional inference cost vs. target baseline, we need to document that in the SLA amendment — finance should review.

I attached a quick telemetry checklist to this email for instrumentation confirmation. Jordan — can infra/product confirm we can implement the dual-signal gating in runtime (kernel-level metrics + request-level traces) and also enforce the mandatory 60-minute pin? If yes, I’ll mark this as pre-approved pending the signed DocuSign.

Laura Bennett
Head of Trust | Redwood Inference

Attachments: telemetry-checklist.xlsx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@fastpay.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T15:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FastPay canary — request for auto-pause + pin as SLA guard

All — sign-off from product/ops side. Implementation notes and final conditions below:

- Approved: temporary kill-switch (automatic pause + version pin) for FastPay canary; window: first 72 hours post-deploy (UTC 2026-10-14 00:00 to 2026-10-17 00:00).
- Trigger logic: dual-signal gating as Laura suggested (require either: a) sustained P95 > 850ms for 3m OR b) 5xx > 0.3% for 5m AND telemetry anomaly flag).
- Action: immediate traffic switch to last-stable variant + enforced 60-minute pin. Pin release requires either: a) signed approval via the DocuSign amendment, b) a thumbs-up from FastPay SRE in the monitoring channel, or c) an Ops-runbook-confirmed remediation.
- Safety nets: automatic alert to both FastPay on-call and Redwood infra on-call; sandboxed replay logs available for the incident window; backoff hysteresis (no re-trigger within 2 hours unless manually overridden).

I’ve created JIRA INF-4821 to track rollout instrumentation and the runtime change. Ops will push a small runtime guard this week to support the gating. Marissa — once the DocuSign is signed, I’ll create the temporary policy and tag the canary for FastPay.

Jordan Blake
Sr. Product Ops | Redwood Inference
